questions.stemHtml: Which of the following Ligament is derived from the marked structure?
questions.solutionHtml:
Falciform Ligament
  • The falciform ligament is the thin, sickle-shaped, fibrous structure that connects the anterior part of the liver to the ventral wall of the abdomen. It can be seen drooping from the liver hilum when looking inside the abdomen during surgery.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 3, Page No. 317., Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery, 7th Edition By PL Dhingra, Page No. 9.

questions.stemHtml: Identify the bone shown in the image?
questions.solutionHtml:
Incus

The incus or anvil is a bone in the middle ear. The anvil-shaped small bone is one of three ossicles in the middle ear. The incus receives vibrations from the malleus, to which it is connected laterally, and transmits these to the stapes medially. The incus is so-called because of its resemblance to an anvil.





BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 3, Page No.224,225., Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 3166.

questions.stemHtml: A patient complains of headache with periorbital pain, photophobia, tearing, lacrimation, drooling of saliva, jaw spasm, pain, with light and accommodation reflex normal and pupils neither dilated nor constricted. Features of the patient can be explained by the involvement of which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
C
  • The given clinical features of headache with periorbital pain, photophobia, tearing lacrimation, drooling of saliva, jaw spasm, pain, with light and accommodation reflex normal and pupils neither dilated nor constricted represents Involvement of trigeminal nerve .

Cranial cavity showing the nerves emerging out

 

Option C is Trigeminal nerve, therefore it is the correct answer.




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 3, Page No.169,170.
